3D points, lines and polygons with depth and time

Source: R/AllClasses.R, R/vector3d.R
SpatVector3D-class.Rd

A SpatVector3D holds features of one geometry type, reported by geomtype(): "points" (a detection at 35 m), "lines" (a dive track or a vessel route) or "polygons" (a marine protected area from 0 to 200 m). Coordinates are longitude and latitude (WGS84), depths are positive metres downward, and times are UTC. Build one with as_vector3d() from a table, sf object or terra::SpatVector.

Usage

# S4 method for class 'SpatVector3D'
geomtype(x, ...)

# S4 method for class 'SpatVector3D'
length(x)

# S4 method for class 'SpatVector3D'
show(object)

# S3 method for class 'SpatVector3D'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

x

A SpatVector3D.

...

Not used.

object

A SpatVector3D.

row.names, optional

Not used.

Value

as.data.frame(): the vertex table for points and lines, or the polygon table, with its sf geometry column, for polygons.

Details

Points and lines have a depth and optional time at each vertex. Polygons have one depth range (depth_min to depth_max) and an optional time interval for the whole shape.

It is the vector counterpart of SpatVoxel and SpatEnvelope. Points and lines are not stored as terra::SpatVector or sf objects: those keep attributes per feature, so a line's depth and time at each vertex would not survive their operations. A polygon's depth range and time are per feature, so polygons keep their outlines in an sf geometry column.

Slots

type

"points", "lines" or "polygons".

vertices

Points and lines: a data frame with one row per vertex: feature_id, vertex (the order within the feature), lon, lat, depth, time (POSIXct, UTC, or NA when the features have no time), and any other columns from the input. Empty for polygons.

features

Polygons: a data frame with one row per polygon: feature_id, depth_min, depth_max, time_start and time_end (POSIXct, UTC, or NA when the polygons have no time; with time_resolution "daily", the interval includes all of the end day), geometry (an sf geometry column of POLYGON or MULTIPOLYGON, EPSG:4326), and any other columns from the input. Empty for points and lines.

time_resolution

"daily" or "datetime" for the precision of the times, as for extract_to_point(), or NA when there is no time.

See also

as_vector3d(), geomtype()

Examples

obs <- data.frame(lon = c(150, 151), lat = c(-20, -21), depth = c(10, 35))
pts <- as_vector3d(obs)
geomtype(pts)
#> [1] "points"
pts
#> class      : SpatVector3D
#> geometry   : points 
#> features   : 2 
#> vertices   : 2 
#> depth (m)  : 10 to 35 
#> time       : none
